source_text: Ἄχρηστον γὰρ ἀληθῶς ἡ παντελὴς σιωπὴ, ὑπὸ πιθανῷ τῷ τοῦ μὴ δύνασθαι ἄξιόν τι λέγειν προκαλύμματι, εὐγνώμων δὲ ἡ πεῖρα ἡ πρὸς τὰς ἀμοιβὰς ἀεὶ, κἂν ἥττων τῆς ἀξίας δύναμις τοῦ τὴν χάριν ἀναφέροντος ᾖ. οὐ γὰρ εἰ μὴ κατ᾽ ἀξίαν οἷός τέ εἰμι λέγειν σιωπήσομαι· ἀλλ᾽ εἰ ἀποπλήσω πάνθ᾽ ἅ μοι δυνατόν ἐστι, καὶ σεμνυνοῦμαι. ἔστω δή μοι ὁ λόγος ὅδε χαριστήριος, Θεῷ μὲν τῷ τῶν ὅλων, οὐκ ἂν ἐθελήσαιμι λέγειν. καίτοι γε ἐκεῖθεν ἡμῖν πᾶσαι μὲν αἱ τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀρχαὶ, ἐκεῖθεν δὲ καὶ ἡμᾶς τῶν εὐχαριστιῶν ἢ ὕμνων καὶ αἴνων, ἄρχεσθαι χρή. ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐδ᾽ εἰ ὅλον ἐμαυτὸν, μὴ οἷος μὲν νῦν εἰμι βέβηλος καὶ ἀκάθαρτος, ἀναμεμιγμένος καὶ πεφυρμένος παναγεῖ, καὶ ἀκαθάρτῳ κακῷ· γυμνὸν δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι καθαρώτατον λαμπρότατόν τε καὶ εἰλικρινέστατον, καὶ ἀμιγῆ παντὸς χείρονος· οὐδ᾽ εἰ ὅλον φημὶ γυμνὸν, ὥσπερ τινὰ γινόμενον φέρων ἐπιδοίην, φέροιμι ἄν τι παρ᾽ ἐμαυτοῦ δῶρον ἄξιον εἰς τιμὴν καὶ ἀμοιβὴν τῷ πάντων ἡγεμόνι καὶ αἰτίῳ· ὃν οὔτε ἰδίᾳ ἕκαστος πώποτε, οὔτε καὶ ἅμα πάντες, ὡσεὶ ἓν καὶ ταὐτὸ γένοιντο πάντα καθαρά· αὑτῶν μὲν ἐκστάντα, πρὸς αὐτὸν δὲ ἐπιστρέψαντα μᾶλλον, ἀθρόα ἑνὶ πνεύματι, καὶ μιᾷ ὁρμῇ τῇ συμφωνίᾳ ἀξίως ἂν εὐφημῆσαι δύναιντο. ὅτι γὰρ τῶν αὐτοῦ δημιουργημάτων καὶ διανοηθῆναί τις ἄριστα καὶ ὁλοκλήρως, καὶ εἰ οἷόν τε εἰπεῖν, κατ᾽ ἀξίαν περὶ αὐτοῦ δυνηθείη· αὐτῆς δὲ τῆς δυνάμεως ἕνεκεν ἧς ἠξίωται οὐ παρ᾽ ἄλλου του, παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ δὲ λαβὼν, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅπως ἂν ἄλλο τι μεῖζον ποθὲν εὐπορήσας εἰς εὐχαριστίαν ἀναθείη.
thought_title: No one can thank God as he deserves
orientation: Silence helps no one; Gregory will give what thanks he can, knowing that no one can thank God worthily.
pass_a_gloss: For truly useless the total silence, under the plausible screen, cover of not being able to say anything worthy; but grateful, right-minded the attempt toward returns always, even if the δύναμις of the one returning the favor be less than the merit. For not, if I cannot speak κατ᾽ ἀξίαν, shall I be silent; but if I fulfill all that is δυνατόν to me, I shall even take pride. Let this λόγος be to me a thank-offering — to the God of the universe I would not wish to say. And yet from there all the beginnings of goods, from there also we must begin the εὐχαριστίαι or hymns and praises. But not even if my whole self — not as I am now, profane and impure, mixed up and soiled with παναγεῖ [printed; sense 'foul', Latin 'tetro'] and impure evil, but bare as purest, brightest, most unmixed, sincere, and unmixed with everything worse — not even if, I say, whole and bare, as one γινόμενον [printed; sense 'newly born', Latin 'velut recens natum'] bringing I should give, could I bring from myself a gift ἄξιον for honor and repayment to the ruler and cause of all; whom neither each individually ever, nor all together, as if all became one and the same, all pure, standing out of themselves, turning rather to him, all at once in one spirit and one impulse of harmony, could worthily praise. For ὅτι [read ὅ,τι: whatever] of his creatures might be able to conceive best and completely, and if possible to speak κατ᾽ ἀξίαν about him — yet for the very δύναμις of which it was deemed worthy, receiving it not from another but from him, there is no way that, finding something greater from anywhere, it could dedicate it εἰς εὐχαριστίαν.

pass_b_english: For total silence is truly useless, hiding behind the plausible excuse of being unable to say anything worthy, while the attempt to make some return is always the mark of a grateful mind, even if the power of the one returning the favor falls short of what is deserved. For I will not keep silent because I cannot speak as the subject deserves. Rather, if I fulfill all that is in my power, I shall even take pride in it.

Let this speech of mine, then, be a thank-offering. I would not presume to say that it is offered to the God of the universe, although it is from him that all the beginnings of good things come to us, and it is with him too that we ought to begin our thanksgivings, hymns and praises. But even if I offered my whole self, not as I am now, profane and impure, mixed and soiled with a foul and unclean evil, but my very self laid bare, as pure, bright and clean as could be, unmixed with anything worse; even if, I say, I brought and gave my whole self bare, as though I were newly born, I could still bring no gift of my own worthy to honor and repay the Ruler and Cause of all. No one could ever praise him worthily, neither each person on his own, nor all together, not even if all things became, as it were, one and the same, all pure, going out of themselves and turning instead to him, gathered in one spirit and with one impulse, in harmony.

For even if any of his creatures could think of him in the best and fullest way, and could, if it may be said, speak of him as he deserves, still, for that very power, which he has been granted, receiving it not from anyone else but from him, there is no way he could find anything greater anywhere to offer in thanks.
notes: 'παναγεῖ' as printed normally means 'all-holy', which cannot stand beside ἀκαθάρτῳ κακῷ; the English takes the sense 'foul', following the Vossius Latin column 'tetro atque immundo malo' (checked on the page image, PDF 77). Doubtful reading. 'ὥσπερ τινὰ γινόμενον' (as printed) is rendered 'as though I were newly born', following the Latin column 'nudum me velut recens natum offeram' (page image checked). The last sentence's opening 'ὅτι' is read as ὅ,τι ('whatever [creature]'), giving 'even if any of his creatures'. 'I would not presume to say that it is offered to the God of the universe' keeps the negation of 'οὐκ ἂν ἐθελήσαιμι λέγειν': Gregory declines to call his speech a thank-offering to God himself (he gives that task to the Word in 4.1). 'In one spirit' (ἑνὶ πνεύματι) means unanimity, not the Holy Spirit; lower case kept. Possible echo of Philippians 1:27 ('in one spirit'), too loose to cite.
